catalog_quote: [Pangloss Lakon corpus presentation, sec. 3.1 'Phonology, orthography'] Lakon has 8 vowel qualities, as well as contrastive vowel length – e.g. pō [pʊ] ‘bamboo’ ≠ pōō [pʊː] ‘to swell’ (François 2005:461). Its vowel system can thus be analyzed as having 16 phonemes in total [Table 2]. Stress is word-final. [François 2005:451] The loss of word-final posttonic vowels explains why, in essentially all the languages of the area, words are now systematically stressed on their final rather than their penultimate syllable (contra Lynch 2000:77). Exactly the same evolution is attested in modern French: due to the progressive loss of all etymological posttonic vowels, French has become a perfectly oxytone language.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Both deciding quotations are verified verbatim in copies we hold at the stated locations (Pangloss sec. 3.1; François 2005:451). The classification (fixed final stress, no secondary-stress statement, no exceptions stated) matches exactly what the sources say: the fieldworker's Lakon-specific sentence 'Stress is word-final.' plus his areal statement that essentially all Torres-Banks languages became oxytone after post-tonic vowel loss, with the only stated deviation concerning Dorig, not Lakon. The source is thin in depth (one sentence in a web sketch, no acoustic or metrical detail) but it is first-hand, recent (2022), by the only modern fieldworker, and nothing better exists — Glottolog has zero descriptive works beyond Codrington's 1885 6-page sketch (silent on accent), and the author's own site confirms he has published no Lakon grammar or dictionary.
